subject.title: [Feature]: Move away from useMultiFileAuthState for Baileys

question: Should WhatsApp authentication use plugin-owned tables in the shared state database or a dedicated WhatsApp SQLite database, and what verified migration and legacy-file cleanup policy should protect existing linked sessions?
rationale: The implementation gap and upstream production warning are clear, but the permanent owner of sensitive credentials, transaction model, backup retention, and upgrade guarantees require explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Shared Plugin SQLite
options.body: Use plugin-owned tables or KV in the shared state database, migrate each configured auth directory through doctor in one verified transaction, and remove legacy runtime reads afterward.

options.title: Dedicated WhatsApp SQLite
options.body: Use a dedicated database only if measured Signal-key volume, locking, backup, or account-lifecycle requirements cannot safely fit the shared state database.

options.title: Retain Hardened Files
options.body: Continue file-backed persistence with narrower durability and security hardening while explicitly accepting Baileys' production limitation.

recommendation.title: Shared Plugin SQLite
recommendation.body: Use plugin-owned tables or KV in the shared state database, migrate each configured auth directory through doctor in one verified transaction, and remove legacy runtime reads afterward.

likelyOwner.reason: The most substantial recent merged work on WhatsApp authentication persistence, recovery, and runtime reconciliation is tied to this contributor.
